jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Mauritania governs AI mainly through its National AI Strategy 2025-2029, published in July 2024 by the digital ministry, and through the 2017 personal data protection law, which bans decisions based solely on automated processing. There is no AI law, no regulator guidance on AI and no public-sector AI rule yet. A Digital and AI Compact is being prepared with the World Bank.
lead_institutions: Ministry of Digital Transformation, Innovation and Modernization of Administration
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from documents read in full on the digital ministry's site and in the Official Journal. The National Assembly's, the cybersecurity agency's and the health ministry's websites could not be accessed. The Digital and AI Compact and the planned AI sub-committee of the High Digital Council are tracked as leads.

instruments.official_title: Loi n°2017-020 du 22 juillet 2017 sur la protection des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 2017-020 of 22 July 2017 on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.current_status: In force. Published in Journal Officiel No. 1400 of 15 November 2017. The text sets no separate commencement date and gives existing processing two or three years to regularise (Arts. 99-100), so effective_date is left null. The Authority was organised by Decree No. 2022-013 of 18 February 2022 and its members were appointed in May 2022.
instruments.summary: Mauritania's general personal data protection law, covering automated and non-automated processing by public and private controllers, with consent, purpose and security principles, rules on cross-border transfers, prior declaration and authorisation formalities, and data-subject rights. Article 19 bars any court decision assessing a person's behaviour, and any decision producing legal effects on a person, from being based solely on automated processing intended to profile the person or evaluate aspects of their personality. It creates the independent Personal Data Protection Authority (Art. 64), attached to the Prime Minister, and sets criminal penalties.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Binding rule on solely automated decisions and profiling; governs personal data used to train and run AI systems.
instruments.publisher_name: Ministry in charge of the General Secretariat of the Government
metadata_gaps: No explicit entry-into-force date in the text

coverage_audit.no_material_found_note: Mauritania's official gazette database, the digital ministry, other ministries and regulators were searched in French and Arabic. No AI law, AI decree or public-sector AI guideline was found, and there was no material for risk and assurance, public-sector use, procurement, cybersecurity, transparency, standards, sandboxes, indices, generative AI or international instruments. The National Assembly, the cybersecurity agency and the health ministry websites were unavailable, and whether the AI strategy was formally adopted by the Council of Ministers remains to be checked.
coverage_audit.technical_note: Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. assembleenationale.mr, ancce.gov.mr proxy 502; sante.gov.mr TLS failure. Strategy undated; 2024-07 from file names/upload dates (no event). Arabic version as source; English same-date version noted. No Council of Ministers adoption act found. Gazette FR/AR AI searches: 0 hits. Open data strategy 2023: no AI. Convention 108 act not found. Units covered: Law: Official gazette legal-text database (msgg.gov.mr) searched in French and Arabic: no AI law, AI decree or AI provision found; Law 2017-020 on personal data protection (Art. 19 automated decisions) recorded from JO 1400. No AI bill found (National Assembly site unreachable). Cybercrime Law 2016-007 and the 2022 data-retention decree have no AI provisions in their titles (not opened). No Convention 108 accession act found.; Government: Ministry of Digital Transformation site and media library searched: National AI Strategy 2025-2029 (final, Arabic and English) and April 2024 draft recorded; Digital and AI Compact in preparation (lead). Open data strategy (June 2023) and digital agenda one-pagers have no AI-specific rules (not recorded). No public-sector AI or generative-AI guideline, procurement rule, algorithm register, sandbox or national AI standard found.; Ministries: Higher education (mesrs.gov.mr) homepage: only news of an AI-in-agriculture workshop, no AI document. Education ministry homepage: nothing found. Health ministry site unreachable. Justice, defence, finance, labour, interior: a general ministry web search surfaced no AI documents; sites not individually searched.; Regulators: Data protection authority (apd.mr): site search and decisions list checked, no AI guidance or AI decision (decisions cover video surveillance and HR processing). Telecom regulator (are.mr) and central bank (bcm.mr): site search, nothing found. National cybersecurity agency (ANCCE, created by Decree 2024-109): site unreachable, not otherwise searched.. Not reached: assembleenationale.mr (proxy 502); ancce.gov.mr (proxy 502); sante.gov.mr (TLS connection failure). Could not verify: Whether the AI strategy was formally adopted by the Council of Ministers (no adoption act found in the gazette).; National Assembly, ANCCE and health ministry sites unreachable.. risk-assurance, public-sector, procurement, cyber-security, transparency, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, generative-ai, international: no material found.
